LECTURE 10 Stage 2: Tokenization & Data

Token Embeddings

Transforming discrete tokens into rich, continuous vector representations that capture meaning
45 min read Hands-on coding Intermediate

Why Do We Need Embeddings?

In our previous lectures, we built a tokenizer that converts raw text into sequences of integer token IDs. For example, the sentence "The cat sat on the mat" might become [464, 3797, 3332, 319, 262, 2603]. But here is the fundamental problem: integers are terrible at representing meaning.

Consider these token IDs: cat = 3797 and dog = 3290. The difference 3797 - 3290 = 507 tells us absolutely nothing about the relationship between cats and dogs. Meanwhile, cat = 3797 and banana = 3820 have a difference of only 23, which might suggest they are closely related — but they clearly are not! Token IDs are arbitrary labels assigned during vocabulary construction. They carry zero semantic information.

Neural networks work with continuous numbers and learn through gradient descent. They need inputs where similar things have similar representations, and where small changes in the input produce small, meaningful changes in output. Integers simply cannot provide this.

Analogy: GPS Coordinates for Words

Think of embeddings as giving each word a GPS coordinate in meaning-space. In the real world, Paris and Lyon are geographically close because they are both in France. Similarly, in embedding space, "king" and "queen" would be nearby because they share the concept of royalty. The key insight: similar meanings → nearby coordinates.

What Are Embeddings? Dense Vector Representations

An embedding is a dense vector of floating-point numbers that represents a token. Instead of a single integer like 3797, the word "cat" might be represented as a vector of, say, 256 numbers:

# Instead of: cat = 3797 (a single meaningless integer)
# We get: cat = [0.12, -0.84, 0.33, ..., 0.07] (256 meaningful floats)

Each dimension in this vector captures some abstract aspect of the word's meaning. While individual dimensions are not directly interpretable (dimension 47 does not literally mean "animal-ness"), the combination of all dimensions together encodes rich semantic information.

The key properties of good embeddings:

Fixed Dimensionality

Every token gets the same number of dimensions (e.g., 256, 512, or 768), regardless of the word length or complexity.

Continuous Values

Values are real numbers (floats), enabling smooth gradients and continuous optimization during training.

Learned Representations

Embeddings are not hand-crafted. The neural network learns the best values through training on data.

Semantic Geometry

Words with similar meanings cluster together; relationships become geometric operations (vector arithmetic).

One-Hot Encoding vs. Dense Embeddings

Before embeddings became standard, one common approach was one-hot encoding: represent each token as a vector where exactly one position is 1 and all others are 0. If our vocabulary has 50,000 tokens, each token becomes a 50,000-dimensional vector with a single 1 in it.

Property One-Hot Encoding Dense Embeddings
Dimensionality Vocabulary size (e.g., 50,257) Chosen size (e.g., 256, 768)
Sparsity Extremely sparse (99.998% zeros) Dense (all values meaningful)
Memory Wasteful: 50K floats per token Efficient: 256–768 floats per token
Similarity All pairs equally distant Similar words are nearby
Learned? No — fixed by definition Yes — trained with the model

Let us see both approaches in code:

Python
import numpy as np

# Our mini vocabulary
vocab = {"the": 0, "cat": 1, "sat": 2, "dog": 3, "mat": 4}
vocab_size = len(vocab)

# === ONE-HOT ENCODING ===
def one_hot_encode(token_id, vocab_size):
 """Create a one-hot vector for a token."""
 vec = np.zeros(vocab_size)
 vec[token_id] = 1.0
 return vec

cat_onehot = one_hot_encode(vocab["cat"], vocab_size)
dog_onehot = one_hot_encode(vocab["dog"], vocab_size)
mat_onehot = one_hot_encode(vocab["mat"], vocab_size)

print("=== One-Hot Encoding ===")
print(f"cat: {cat_onehot}")
print(f"dog: {dog_onehot}")
print(f"mat: {mat_onehot}")

# Cosine similarity between one-hot vectors
def cosine_sim(a, b):
 dot = np.dot(a, b)
 norm = np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b)
 return dot / norm if norm != 0 else 0.0

print(f"\
Similarity(cat, dog) = {cosine_sim(cat_onehot, dog_onehot):.4f}")
print(f"Similarity(cat, mat) = {cosine_sim(cat_onehot, mat_onehot):.4f}")
print("Problem: ALL pairs have similarity 0 — no relationships captured!")

The Embedding Matrix: A Lookup Table

At its core, an embedding layer is simply a lookup table stored as a matrix. If we have a vocabulary of V tokens and we choose an embedding dimension of d, then our embedding matrix W has shape (V, d).

When we want the embedding for token ID i, we simply look up row i of the matrix. That is it — no complex computation, just a table lookup.

Embedding Lookup Visualization

Token IDs: [ 2, 0, 4, 1 ]
 | | | |
 v v v v
 ┌─────────────────────────────┐
 Row 0 ──── │ 0.12 -0.31 0.55 0.08 │ ← "the"
 Row 1 ──── │ -0.84 0.22 0.67 -0.15 │ ← "cat"
 Row 2 ──── │ 0.33 0.91 -0.44 0.72 │ ← "sat"
 Row 3 ──── │ -0.71 0.18 0.59 -0.22 │ ← "dog"
 Row 4 ──── │ 0.05 -0.63 0.11 0.88 │ ← "mat"
 └─────────────────────────────┘
 Embedding Matrix W (5 x 4)

Output: [row2, row0, row4, row1]
 Shape: (4, 4) — 4 tokens, each with 4-dim embedding

Let us build this manually:

Python
import numpy as np

# Our mini vocabulary
vocab = {"the": 0, "cat": 1, "sat": 2, "dog": 3, "mat": 4}
vocab_size = len(vocab)
embed_dim = 4 # Small dimension for demonstration

# Create a random embedding matrix (in practice, this is learned)
np.random.seed(42)
embedding_matrix = np.random.randn(vocab_size, embed_dim) * 0.1

print("Embedding Matrix (shape: {}):".format(embedding_matrix.shape))
for word, idx in sorted(vocab.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]):
 print(f" {word:<5} (id={idx}): {embedding_matrix[idx]}")

# Lookup: convert token IDs to embeddings
token_ids = [vocab["the"], vocab["cat"], vocab["sat"]]
print(f"\
Token IDs: {token_ids}")

# The lookup is just array indexing!
embeddings = embedding_matrix[token_ids]
print(f"Embeddings shape: {embeddings.shape}")
print(f"Embeddings:\
{embeddings}")

# Key insight: this is just matrix row selection
print(f"\
Direct lookup for 'cat' (id=1): {embedding_matrix[1]}")
print(f"Same as indexing: {embedding_matrix[vocab['cat']]}")
Key Insight

An embedding lookup is mathematically equivalent to multiplying a one-hot vector by the embedding matrix: one_hot @ W = W[token_id]. But direct indexing is far more efficient — we skip the multiplication entirely and just grab the right row. This is why frameworks provide dedicated Embedding layers rather than using matrix multiplication.

Building a PyTorch-Style Embedding Layer

In PyTorch, you would use nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim). Let us build our own version from scratch to understand exactly what happens inside:

Python
import numpy as np

class Embedding:
 """A simple embedding layer, similar to PyTorch's nn.Embedding."""

 def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
 """
 Args:
 num_embeddings: Size of the vocabulary (V)
 embedding_dim: Dimension of each embedding vector (d)
 """
 self.num_embeddings = num_embeddings
 self.embedding_dim = embedding_dim
 # Initialize weights randomly (Xavier/Glorot-like initialization)
 scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
 self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale

 def forward(self, token_ids):
 """
 Look up embeddings for the given token IDs.

 Args:
 token_ids: list or array of integer token IDs
 Returns:
 numpy array of shape (len(token_ids), embedding_dim)
 """
 return self.weight[token_ids]

 def __repr__(self):
 return f"Embedding({self.num_embeddings}, {self.embedding_dim})"

# === Demo: Using our Embedding layer ===
np.random.seed(123)

# GPT-2 uses vocab_size=50257, embed_dim=768
# We will use smaller values for demonstration
vocab_size = 10
embed_dim = 6

emb_layer = Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
print(f"Layer: {emb_layer}")
print(f"Weight matrix shape: {emb_layer.weight.shape}")

# Simulate a tokenized sentence: "The cat sat on the mat"
token_ids = [2, 5, 7, 3, 2, 8]
print(f"\
Token IDs: {token_ids}")

# Get embeddings
output = emb_layer.forward(token_ids)
print(f"Output shape: {output.shape}")
print(f"\
Embedding for token 2 (first occurrence): {output[0].round(3)}")
print(f"Embedding for token 2 (second occurrence): {output[4].round(3)}")
print(f"Same token = same embedding: {np.allclose(output[0], output[4])}")

# In GPT-2:
print(f"\
--- GPT-2 Scale ---")
print(f"Vocabulary size: 50,257 tokens")
print(f"Embedding dimension: 768")
print(f"Embedding matrix parameters: {50257 * 768:,} = ~38.6 million!")

Embedding Dimensions and Their Meaning

The embedding dimension (d) is a crucial hyperparameter. It determines how much information each token embedding can carry. Common choices in practice:

Model Embedding Dim Vocab Size Embedding Parameters
GPT-2 Small 768 50,257 38.6M
GPT-2 Medium 1,024 50,257 51.5M
GPT-2 Large 1,280 50,257 64.3M
GPT-3 12,288 50,257 617.6M

Higher dimensions allow the model to capture more nuanced relationships, but they also increase memory usage and computation time. Think of it like the resolution of a photograph: more pixels capture more detail, but at the cost of file size.

How Embeddings Capture Semantic Relationships

After training, embeddings develop remarkable properties. The most famous example is the king–queen analogy:

vector("king") - vector("man") + vector("woman") ≈ vector("queen")

This works because the embedding space organizes concepts along meaningful directions. The difference king - man captures the concept of "royalty," and adding it to woman gives us the female royal equivalent.

Python
import numpy as np

# Simulated pre-trained embeddings (simplified 4D for illustration)
# In reality these would be learned from billions of words
np.random.seed(42)

# We manually construct embeddings that demonstrate the analogy
# Dimensions loosely represent: [royalty, gender, age, animate]
embeddings = {
 "king": np.array([ 0.9, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9]),
 "queen": np.array([ 0.9, 0.9, 0.5, 0.9]),
 "man": np.array([ 0.1, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9]),
 "woman": np.array([ 0.1, 0.9, 0.5, 0.9]),
 "prince": np.array([ 0.8, 0.1, 0.1, 0.9]),
 "cat": np.array([-0.5, -0.2, 0.3, 0.8]),
 "dog": np.array([-0.5, -0.1, 0.3, 0.8]),
 "table": np.array([-0.8, -0.5, 0.0, -0.9]),
}

def cosine_sim(a, b):
 return np.dot(a, b) / (np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b))

# The famous analogy: king - man + woman = ?
result = embeddings["king"] - embeddings["man"] + embeddings["woman"]
print("=== King - Man + Woman = ? ===")
print(f"Result vector: {result}")
print(f"Queen vector: {embeddings['queen']}")
print(f"Similarity to queen: {cosine_sim(result, embeddings['queen']):.4f}")

# Find the closest word to the result
print("\
=== Closest words to result ===")
for word, vec in embeddings.items():
 sim = cosine_sim(result, vec)
 print(f" {word:<8} similarity: {sim:.4f}")

# Show that similar concepts cluster
print("\
=== Semantic Similarities ===")
pairs = [("king", "queen"), ("cat", "dog"), ("king", "table"),
 ("man", "woman"), ("cat", "table")]
for w1, w2 in pairs:
 sim = cosine_sim(embeddings[w1], embeddings[w2])
 print(f" sim({w1:<6}, {w2:<6}) = {sim:.4f}")

Visualizing Embeddings in 2D

While real embeddings live in hundreds of dimensions, we can project them down to 2D to visualize the clustering structure. Techniques like PCA (Principal Component Analysis) or t-SNE are commonly used for this. Here is a simple PCA-based visualization approach:

Embedding Space (Conceptual 2D Projection)

 Royalty ↑
 | queen * * king
 |
 | woman * * man
 |
 |
 | * cat
 | * dog
 |
 ─────────┼──────────────────────────→ Gender
 |
 | * table
 | * chair
Connection to the Book

In Chapter 2 of "Build an LLM from Scratch," Raschka implements the token embedding layer as the first component of the GPT model. The embedding dimension (d_model or cfg["emb_dim"]) flows through the entire architecture — every subsequent layer (attention, feed-forward) operates on vectors of this same dimension.

Building Embeddings for Our Tokenizer

Let us connect our embedding layer to the BPE tokenizer we built in the previous lectures. This is exactly how GPT-2 processes its input:

Python
import numpy as np

class SimpleTokenizer:
 """Minimal word-level tokenizer for demonstration."""
 def __init__(self, vocab):
 self.str_to_int = vocab
 self.int_to_str = {v: k for k, v in vocab.items()}

 def encode(self, text):
 tokens = text.lower().split()
 return [self.str_to_int.get(t, self.str_to_int.get("<unk>", 0))
 for t in tokens]

 def decode(self, ids):
 return " ".join(self.int_to_str.get(i, "<unk>") for i in ids)

class Embedding:
 def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
 scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
 self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale

 def forward(self, token_ids):
 return self.weight[np.array(token_ids)]

# Step 1: Create a vocabulary
vocab = {
 "<unk>": 0, "<pad>": 1, "the": 2, "cat": 3, "sat": 4,
 "on": 5, "mat": 6, "dog": 7, "ran": 8, "to": 9, "a": 10,
 "big": 11, "small": 12, "red": 13, "blue": 14, "house": 15
}

# Step 2: Initialize tokenizer and embedding layer
np.random.seed(42)
tokenizer = SimpleTokenizer(vocab)
embed_dim = 8
token_embedding = Embedding(len(vocab), embed_dim)

# Step 3: Process text through the pipeline
text = "the big cat sat on a red mat"
print(f"Input text: '{text}'")

token_ids = tokenizer.encode(text)
print(f"Token IDs: {token_ids}")
print(f"Decoded: '{tokenizer.decode(token_ids)}'")

# Step 4: Get embeddings
embeddings = token_embedding.forward(token_ids)
print(f"\
Embeddings shape: {embeddings.shape}")
print(f" (sequence_length={len(token_ids)}, embed_dim={embed_dim})")

print(f"\
First 3 token embeddings:")
for i in range(3):
 word = tokenizer.int_to_str[token_ids[i]]
 print(f" '{word}' (id={token_ids[i]}): {embeddings[i].round(3)}")

print(f"\
--- Pipeline Summary ---")
print(f"Text -> Tokens -> IDs -> Embeddings")
print(f"'{text}'")
print(f" -> {text.lower().split()}")
print(f" -> {token_ids}")
print(f" -> tensor of shape {embeddings.shape}")
Important Note

At initialization, embeddings are random! They do not carry any meaning yet. The magic happens during training, when the model adjusts these vectors through backpropagation to minimize the loss function. After training on enough data, the embeddings naturally organize into the meaningful geometric structure we described.

Summary

Key Takeaways

  • Token IDs are arbitrary integers with no semantic meaning
  • Embeddings are dense vectors that capture word relationships
  • The embedding layer is a simple lookup table (matrix)
  • Embedding dimensions are a key hyperparameter (GPT-2: 768)
  • After training, similar words end up near each other in the embedding space

What is Next

We now have embeddings for each token, but our model has no concept of word order. The embedding for "cat" is the same whether it appears first or last in a sentence. In Lecture 11, we will add positional embeddings to solve this problem.

LECȚIA 10 Etapa 2: Tokenizare & Date

Embedding-uri de Token-uri

Transformarea token-urilor discrete in reprezentari vectoriale continue si bogate care surprind semnificatia
45 min lectură Exerciții practice de cod Intermediar

De ce avem nevoie de embedding-uri?

În lecțiile anterioare, am construit un tokenizer care convertește textul brut în secvențe de ID-uri întregi ale token-urilor. De exemplu, propoziția „The cat sat on the mat” ar putea deveni [464, 3797, 3332, 319, 262, 2603]. Dar iată problema fundamentală: numerele întregi sunt groaznice la reprezentarea semnificației.

Considerați aceste ID-uri de token-uri: cat = 3797 și dog = 3290. Diferența 3797 - 3290 = 507 nu ne spune absolut nimic despre relația dintre pisici și câini. Între timp, cat = 3797 și banana = 3820 au o diferență de doar 23, ceea ce ar putea sugera că sunt strâns înrudite — dar în mod evident nu sunt! ID-urile de token-uri sunt etichete arbitrare atribuite în timpul construcției vocabularului. Nu conțin nicio informație semantică.

Rețelele neuronale lucrează cu numere continue și învață prin coborârea gradientului. Au nevoie de intrări în care lucrurile similare au reprezentări similare și în care modificări mici ale intrării produc modificări mici și semnificative ale ieșirii. Numerele întregi pur și simplu nu pot oferi acest lucru.

Analogie: Coordonate GPS pentru cuvinte

Gândiți-vă la embedding-uri ca oferind fiecărui cuvânt o coordonată GPS în spațiul semnificației. În lumea reală, Parisul și Lyonul sunt apropiate geografic pentru că ambele se află în Franța. În mod similar, în spațiul embedding-urilor, „king” și „queen” ar fi aproape pentru că împart conceptul de regalitate. Ideea cheie: semnificații similare → coordonate apropiate.

Ce sunt embedding-urile? Reprezentări vectoriale dense

Un embedding este un vector dens de numere în virgulă mobilă care reprezintă un token. În loc de un singur întreg precum 3797, cuvântul „cat” ar putea fi reprezentat ca un vector de, să zicem, 256 de numere:

# Instead of: cat = 3797 (a single meaningless integer)
# We get: cat = [0.12, -0.84, 0.33, ..., 0.07] (256 meaningful floats)

Fiecare dimensiune din acest vector surprinde un aspect abstract al semnificației cuvântului. Deși dimensiunile individuale nu sunt direct interpretabile (dimensiunea 47 nu înseamnă literal „grad de animal”), combinația tuturor dimensiunilor codifică împreună informații semantice bogate.

Proprietățile cheie ale unor embedding-uri bune:

Dimensionalitate fixă

Fiecare token primește același număr de dimensiuni (de ex., 256, 512 sau 768), indiferent de lungimea sau complexitatea cuvântului.

Valori continue

Valorile sunt numere reale (float-uri), permițând gradienți linși și optimizare continuă în timpul antrenamentului.

Reprezentări învățate

Embedding-urile nu sunt create manual. Rețeaua neuronală învață cele mai bune valori prin antrenament pe date.

Geometrie semantică

Cuvintele cu semnificații similare se grupează împreună; relațiile devin operații geometrice (aritmetică vectorială).

Codificare One-Hot vs. Embedding-uri dense

Înainte ca embedding-urile să devină standard, o abordare comună era codificarea one-hot: reprezentarea fiecărui token ca un vector în care exact o poziție este 1 și toate celelalte sunt 0. Dacă vocabularul nostru are 50.000 de token-uri, fiecare token devine un vector cu 50.000 de dimensiuni cu un singur 1 în el.

Proprietate Codificare One-Hot Embedding-uri dense
Dimensionalitate Dimensiunea vocabularului (de ex., 50.257) Dimensiune aleasă (de ex., 256, 768)
Raritate Extrem de rară (99,998% zerouri) Densă (toate valorile semnificative)
Memorie Risipitoare: 50K float-uri per token Eficientă: 256–768 float-uri per token
Similaritate Toate perechile la distanță egală Cuvintele similare sunt apropiate
Învățată? Nu — fixă prin definiție Da — antrenată cu modelul

Să vedem ambele abordări în cod:

Python
import numpy as np

# Our mini vocabulary
vocab = {"the": 0, "cat": 1, "sat": 2, "dog": 3, "mat": 4}
vocab_size = len(vocab)

# === ONE-HOT ENCODING ===
def one_hot_encode(token_id, vocab_size):
 """Create a one-hot vector for a token."""
 vec = np.zeros(vocab_size)
 vec[token_id] = 1.0
 return vec

cat_onehot = one_hot_encode(vocab["cat"], vocab_size)
dog_onehot = one_hot_encode(vocab["dog"], vocab_size)
mat_onehot = one_hot_encode(vocab["mat"], vocab_size)

print("=== One-Hot Encoding ===")
print(f"cat: {cat_onehot}")
print(f"dog: {dog_onehot}")
print(f"mat: {mat_onehot}")

# Cosine similarity between one-hot vectors
def cosine_sim(a, b):
 dot = np.dot(a, b)
 norm = np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b)
 return dot / norm if norm != 0 else 0.0

print(f"\
Similarity(cat, dog) = {cosine_sim(cat_onehot, dog_onehot):.4f}")
print(f"Similarity(cat, mat) = {cosine_sim(cat_onehot, mat_onehot):.4f}")
print("Problem: ALL pairs have similarity 0 — no relationships captured!")

Matricea de embedding: un tabel de căutare

În esență, un strat de embedding este pur și simplu un tabel de căutare stocat ca matrice. Dacă avem un vocabular de V token-uri și alegem o dimensiune de embedding de d, atunci matricea noastră de embedding W are forma (V, d).

Când dorim embedding-ul pentru ID-ul de token i, pur și simplu căutăm rândul i din matrice. Atât — nicio calculă complexă, doar o căutare în tabel.

Vizualizarea căutării embedding-ului

Token IDs: [ 2, 0, 4, 1 ]
 | | | |
 v v v v
 ┌─────────────────────────────┐
 Row 0 ──── │ 0.12 -0.31 0.55 0.08 │ ← "the"
 Row 1 ──── │ -0.84 0.22 0.67 -0.15 │ ← "cat"
 Row 2 ──── │ 0.33 0.91 -0.44 0.72 │ ← "sat"
 Row 3 ──── │ -0.71 0.18 0.59 -0.22 │ ← "dog"
 Row 4 ──── │ 0.05 -0.63 0.11 0.88 │ ← "mat"
 └─────────────────────────────┘
 Matricea de Embedding W (5 x 4)

Output: [row2, row0, row4, row1]
 Forma: (4, 4) — 4 token-uri, fiecare cu embedding de 4 dimensiuni

Să construim acest lucru manual:

Python
import numpy as np

# Our mini vocabulary
vocab = {"the": 0, "cat": 1, "sat": 2, "dog": 3, "mat": 4}
vocab_size = len(vocab)
embed_dim = 4 # Small dimension for demonstration

# Create a random embedding matrix (in practice, this is learned)
np.random.seed(42)
embedding_matrix = np.random.randn(vocab_size, embed_dim) * 0.1

print("Embedding Matrix (shape: {}):".format(embedding_matrix.shape))
for word, idx in sorted(vocab.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]):
 print(f" {word:<5} (id={idx}): {embedding_matrix[idx]}")

# Lookup: convert token IDs to embeddings
token_ids = [vocab["the"], vocab["cat"], vocab["sat"]]
print(f"\
Token IDs: {token_ids}")

# The lookup is just array indexing!
embeddings = embedding_matrix[token_ids]
print(f"Embeddings shape: {embeddings.shape}")
print(f"Embeddings:\
{embeddings}")

# Key insight: this is just matrix row selection
print(f"\
Direct lookup for 'cat' (id=1): {embedding_matrix[1]}")
print(f"Same as indexing: {embedding_matrix[vocab['cat']]}")
Ideea cheie

O căutare de embedding este matematic echivalentă cu multiplicarea unui vector one-hot cu matricea de embedding: one_hot @ W = W[token_id]. Dar indexarea directă este mult mai eficientă — sărim peste multiplicare și pur și simplu luăm rândul corect. Acesta este motivul pentru care framework-urile oferă straturi dedicate de Embedding în loc să folosească multiplicarea matricială.

Construirea unui strat de embedding în stilul PyTorch

În PyTorch, ați folosi nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim). Să construim propria noastră versiune de la zero pentru a înțelege exact ce se întâmplă în interior:

Python
import numpy as np

class Embedding:
 """A simple embedding layer, similar to PyTorch's nn.Embedding."""

 def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
 """
 Args:
 num_embeddings: Size of the vocabulary (V)
 embedding_dim: Dimension of each embedding vector (d)
 """
 self.num_embeddings = num_embeddings
 self.embedding_dim = embedding_dim
 # Initialize weights randomly (Xavier/Glorot-like initialization)
 scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
 self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale

 def forward(self, token_ids):
 """
 Look up embeddings for the given token IDs.

 Args:
 token_ids: list or array of integer token IDs
 Returns:
 numpy array of shape (len(token_ids), embedding_dim)
 """
 return self.weight[token_ids]

 def __repr__(self):
 return f"Embedding({self.num_embeddings}, {self.embedding_dim})"

# === Demo: Using our Embedding layer ===
np.random.seed(123)

# GPT-2 uses vocab_size=50257, embed_dim=768
# We will use smaller values for demonstration
vocab_size = 10
embed_dim = 6

emb_layer = Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
print(f"Layer: {emb_layer}")
print(f"Weight matrix shape: {emb_layer.weight.shape}")

# Simulate a tokenized sentence: "The cat sat on the mat"
token_ids = [2, 5, 7, 3, 2, 8]
print(f"\
Token IDs: {token_ids}")

# Get embeddings

print(f"Output shape: {output.shape}")

Embedding for token 2 (first occurrence): {output[0].round(3)}")

# In GPT-2:

--- GPT-2 Scale ---")
print(f"Vocabulary size: 50,257 tokens")
print(f"Embedding dimension: 768")
print(f"Embedding matrix parameters: {50257 * 768:,} = ~38.6 million!")

Dimensiunile embedding-ului și semnificația lor

Dimensiunea embedding-ului (d) este un hiperparametru crucial. Determină câtă informație poate conține fiecare embedding de token. Alegeri comune în practică:

Model Dim. embedding Dim. vocabular Parametri embedding
GPT-2 Small 768 50.257 38,6M
GPT-2 Medium 1.024 50.257 51,5M
GPT-2 Large 1.280 50.257 64,3M
GPT-3 12.288 50.257 617,6M

Dimensiunile mai mari permit modelului să surprindă relații mai nuansăte, dar cresc și utilizarea memoriei și timpul de calcul. Gândiți-vă la asta ca la rezoluția unei fotografii: mai mulți pixeli surprind mai multe detalii, dar cu costul dimensiunii fișierului.

Cum surprind embedding-urile relațiile semantice

După antrenament, embedding-urile dezvoltă proprietăți remarcabile. Cel mai faimos exemplu este analogia king–queen:

vector("king") - vector("man") + vector("woman") ≈ vector("queen")

Acest lucru funcționează pentru că spațiul de embedding organizează conceptele de-a lungul unor direcții semnificative. Diferența king - man surprinde conceptul de „regalitate”, iar adăugarea acestuia la woman ne dă echivalentul regal feminin.

Python
import numpy as np

# Simulated pre-trained embeddings (simplified 4D for illustration)
# In reality these would be learned from billions of words
np.random.seed(42)

# We manually construct embeddings that demonstrate the analogy
# Dimensions loosely represent: [royalty, gender, age, animate]
embeddings = {
 "king": np.array([ 0.9, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9]),
 "queen": np.array([ 0.9, 0.9, 0.5, 0.9]),
 "man": np.array([ 0.1, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9]),
 "woman": np.array([ 0.1, 0.9, 0.5, 0.9]),
 "prince": np.array([ 0.8, 0.1, 0.1, 0.9]),
 "cat": np.array([-0.5, -0.2, 0.3, 0.8]),
 "dog": np.array([-0.5, -0.1, 0.3, 0.8]),
 "table": np.array([-0.8, -0.5, 0.0, -0.9]),
}

def cosine_sim(a, b):
 return np.dot(a, b) / (np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b))

# The famous analogy: king - man + woman = ?
result = embeddings["king"] - embeddings["man"] + embeddings["woman"]
print("=== King - Man + Woman = ? ===")
print(f"Result vector: {result}")
print(f"Queen vector: {embeddings['queen']}")
print(f"Similarity to queen: {cosine_sim(result, embeddings['queen']):.4f}")

# Find the closest word to the result
print("\
=== Closest words to result ===")
for word, vec in embeddings.items():
 sim = cosine_sim(result, vec)
 print(f" {word:<8} similarity: {sim:.4f}")

# Show that similar concepts cluster
print("\
=== Semantic Similarities ===")
pairs = [("king", "queen"), ("cat", "dog"), ("king", "table"),
 ("man", "woman"), ("cat", "table")]
for w1, w2 in pairs:
 sim = cosine_sim(embeddings[w1], embeddings[w2])
 print(f" sim({w1:<6}, {w2:<6}) = {sim:.4f}")

Vizualizarea embedding-urilor în 2D

Deși embedding-urile reale trăiesc în sute de dimensiuni, le putem proiecta în 2D pentru a vizualiza structura de grupare. Tehnici precum PCA (Analiza Componentelor Principale) sau t-SNE sunt folosite frecvent pentru aceasta. Iată o abordare simplă de vizualizare bazată pe PCA:

Spațiul embedding-urilor (Proiecție conceptuală 2D)

Legătura cu cartea

În Capitolul 2 al cărții „Build an LLM from Scratch”, Raschka implementează stratul de embedding al token-urilor ca primă componentă a modelului GPT. Dimensiunea embedding-ului (d_model sau cfg["emb_dim"]) se propagă prin întreaga arhitectură — fiecare strat ulterior (atenție, feed-forward) operează pe vectori cu aceeași dimensiune.

Construirea embedding-urilor pentru tokenizer-ul nostru

Să conectăm stratul de embedding la tokenizer-ul BPE pe care l-am construit în lecțiile anterioare. Exact așa procesează GPT-2 intrarea sa:

Python
import numpy as np

class SimpleTokenizer:
 """Minimal word-level tokenizer for demonstration."""
 def __init__(self, vocab):
 self.str_to_int = vocab
 self.int_to_str = {v: k for k, v in vocab.items()}

 def encode(self, text):
 tokens = text.lower().split()
 return [self.str_to_int.get(t, self.str_to_int.get("<unk>", 0))
 for t in tokens]

 def decode(self, ids):
 return " ".join(self.int_to_str.get(i, "<unk>") for i in ids)

class Embedding:
 def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
 scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
 self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale

 def forward(self, token_ids):
 return self.weight[np.array(token_ids)]

# Step 1: Create a vocabulary
vocab = {
 "<unk>": 0, "<pad>": 1, "the": 2, "cat": 3, "sat": 4,
 "on": 5, "mat": 6, "dog": 7, "ran": 8, "to": 9, "a": 10,
 "big": 11, "small": 12, "red": 13, "blue": 14, "house": 15
}

# Step 2: Initialize tokenizer and embedding layer
np.random.seed(42)
tokenizer = SimpleTokenizer(vocab)
embed_dim = 8
token_embedding = Embedding(len(vocab), embed_dim)

# Step 3: Process text through the pipeline
text = "the big cat sat on a red mat"
print(f"Input text: '{text}'")

token_ids = tokenizer.encode(text)
print(f"Token IDs: {token_ids}")
print(f"Decoded: '{tokenizer.decode(token_ids)}'")

# Step 4: Get embeddings
embeddings = token_embedding.forward(token_ids)
print(f"\
Embeddings shape: {embeddings.shape}")
print(f" (sequence_length={len(token_ids)}, embed_dim={embed_dim})")

print(f"\
First 3 token embeddings:")
for i in range(3):
 word = tokenizer.int_to_str[token_ids[i]]
 print(f" '{word}' (id={token_ids[i]}): {embeddings[i].round(3)}")

print(f"\
--- Pipeline Summary ---")
print(f"Text -> Tokens -> IDs -> Embeddings")
print(f"'{text}'")
print(f" -> {text.lower().split()}")
print(f" -> {token_ids}")
print(f" -> tensor of shape {embeddings.shape}")
Notă importantă

La inițializare, embedding-urile sunt aleatorii! Nu conțin încă nicio semnificație. Magia se întâmplă în timpul antrenamentului, când modelul ajustează acești vectori prin retropropagare pentru a minimiza funcția de pierdere. După antrenamentul pe suficiente date, embedding-urile se organizează natural în structura geometrică semnificativă pe care am descris-o.

Rezumat

Idei cheie

  • ID-urile de token-uri sunt numere întregi arbitrare fără semnificație semantică
  • Embedding-urile sunt vectori denși care surprind relațiile dintre cuvinte
  • Stratul de embedding este un simplu tabel de căutare (matrice)
  • Dimensiunile embedding-ului sunt un hiperparametru cheie (GPT-2: 768)
  • După antrenament, cuvintele similare ajung aproape unele de altele în spațiul embedding-urilor

Ce urmează

Acum avem embedding-uri pentru fiecare token, dar modelul nostru nu are niciun concept de ordine a cuvintelor. Embedding-ul pentru „cat” este același indiferent dacă apare primul sau ultimul într-o propoziție. În Lecția 11, vom adăuga embedding-uri poziționale pentru a rezolva această problemă.

45 λεπτα αναγνωση Πρακτικη εξασκηση Μεσαιο

Για παραδειγμα, η προταση "The cat sat on the mat" μπορει να γινει [464, 3797, 3332, 319, 262, 2603]. Αλλα εδω ειναι το θεμελιωδες προβλημα: οι ακεραιοι ειναι αποτυχημενοι στην αναπαρασταση σημασιας.

Σκεφτειτε αυτα τα token IDs: cat = 3797 και dog = 3290. Η διαφορα 3797 - 3290 = 507 δεν μας λεει απολυτως τιποτα για τη σχεση μεταξυ γατας και σκυλων. Εν τω μεταξυ, cat = 3797 και banana = 3820 εχουν διαφορα μονο 23, που θα μπορουσε να υποδηλωνει οτι ειναι στενα συνδεδεμενα — αλλα προφανως δεν ειναι! Τα token IDs ειναι αυθαιρετες ετικετες που ανατιθενται κατα την κατασκευη του λεξιλογιου. Δεν φερουν καμια σημασιολογικη πληροφορια.

Τα νευρωνικα δικτυα λειτουργουν με συνεχεις αριθμους και μαθαινουν μεσω gradient descent. Χρειαζονται εισοδους οπου παρομοια πραγματα εχουν παρομοιες αναπαραστασεις, και οπου μικρες αλλαγες στην εισοδο παραγουν μικρες, σημαντικες αλλαγες στην εξοδο. Οι ακεραιοι απλα δεν μπορουν να το προσφερουν αυτο.

Αναλογια: Συντεταγμενες GPS για Λεξεις

Σκεφτειτε τα embeddings σαν να δινετε σε καθε λεξη μια συντεταγμενη GPS στον χωρο της σημασιας. Στον πραγματικο κοσμο, το Παρισι και η Λυων ειναι γεωγραφικα κοντα επειδη βρισκονται και τα δυο στη Γαλλια. Ομοιως, στον χωρο των embeddings, οι λεξεις "king" και "queen" θα ηταν κοντα επειδη μοιραζονται την εννοια της βασιλειας. Το κλειδι: παρομοιες σημασιες → κοντινες συντεταγμενες.

Τι Ειναι τα Embeddings; Πυκνες Διανυσματικες Αναπαραστασεις

Ενα embedding ειναι ενα πυκνο διανυσμα αριθμων κινητης υποδιαστολης που αναπαριστα ενα token. Αντι για εναν μοναδικο ακεραιο οπως το 3797, η λεξη "cat" μπορει να αναπαρασταθει ως διανυσμα απο, ας πουμε, 256 αριθμους:

# Instead of: cat = 3797 (a single meaningless integer)
# We get: cat = [0.12, -0.84, 0.33, ..., 0.07] (256 meaningful floats)

Καθε διασταση σε αυτο το διανυσμα αποτυπωνει καποια αφηρημενη πτυχη της σημασιας της λεξης. Αν και οι μεμονωμενες διαστασεις δεν ειναι αμεσα ερμηνευσιμες (η διασταση 47 δεν σημαινει κυριολεκτικα "ζωικοτητα"), ο συνδυασμος ολων των διαστασεων μαζι κωδικοποιει πλουσια σημασιολογικη πληροφορια.

Οι βασικες ιδιοτητες καλων embeddings:

Σταθερη Διαστατικοτητα

Καθε token παιρνει τον ιδιο αριθμο διαστασεων (π.χ., 256, 512 η 768), ανεξαρτητα απο το μηκος η την πολυπλοκοτητα της λεξης.

Συνεχεις Τιμες

Οι τιμες ειναι πραγματικοι αριθμοι (floats), επιτρεποντας ομαλες κλισεις και συνεχη βελτιστοποιηση κατα την εκπαιδευση.

Εκπαιδευμενες Αναπαραστασεις

Τα embeddings δεν κατασκευαζονται χειροκινητα. Το νευρωνικο δικτυο μαθαινει τις καλυτερες τιμες μεσω εκπαιδευσης σε δεδομενα.

Σημασιολογικη Γεωμετρια

Λεξεις με παρομοια σημασια ομαδοποιουνται μαζι· οι σχεσεις γινονται γεωμετρικες πραξεις (διανυσματικη αριθμητικη).

One-Hot Encoding εναντιον Πυκνων Embeddings

Πριν τα embeddings γινουν προτυπο, μια συνηθισμενη προσεγγιση ηταν το one-hot encoding: αναπαραστησε καθε token ως διανυσμα οπου ακριβως μια θεση ειναι 1 και ολες οι αλλες ειναι 0. Αν το λεξιλογιο μας εχει 50.000 tokens, καθε token γινεται ενα διανυσμα 50.000 διαστασεων με εναν μοναδικο ασσο σε αυτο.

Ιδιοτητα One-Hot Encoding Πυκνα Embeddings
Διαστατικοτητα Μεγεθος λεξιλογιου (π.χ., 50.257) Επιλεγμενο μεγεθος (π.χ., 256, 768)
Αραιοτητα Εξαιρετικα αραιο (99,998% μηδενικα) Πυκνο (ολες οι τιμες σημαντικες)
Μνημη Σπαταλη: 50K floats ανα token Αποδοτικο: 256–768 floats ανα token
Ομοιοτητα Ολα τα ζευγη εξισου απεχουν Παρομοιες λεξεις ειναι κοντα
Εκπαιδευμενο; Οχι — καθορισμενο εξ ορισμου Ναι — εκπαιδευεται με το μοντελο

Ας δουμε και τις δυο προσεγγισεις σε κωδικα:

# Our mini vocabulary

def one_hot_encode(token_id, vocab_size):

cat_onehot = one_hot_encode(vocab["cat"], vocab_size)

Ο Πινακας Embedding: Ενας Πινακας Αναζητησης

Στον πυρηνα του, ενα στρωμα embedding ειναι απλα ενας πινακας αναζητησης αποθηκευμενος ως πινακας. Αν εχουμε λεξιλογιο V tokens και επιλεξουμε διασταση embedding d, τοτε ο πινακας embedding W εχει σχημα (V, d).

Οταν θελουμε το embedding για το token ID i, απλα αναζητουμε την γραμμη i του πινακα. Αυτο ειναι ολο — κανενας πολυπλοκος υπολογισμος, απλα μια αναζητηση πινακα.

Μια αναζητηση embedding ειναι μαθηματικα ισοδυναμη με τον πολλαπλασιασμο ενος one-hot διανυσματος με τον πινακα embedding: one_hot @ W = W[token_id]. Αλλα η απευθειας ευρετηριαση ειναι πολυ πιο αποδοτικη — παρακαμπτουμε εντελως τον πολλαπλασιασμο και απλα παιρνουμε τη σωστη γραμμη. Γι αυτο τα frameworks παρεχουν ειδικα στρωματα Embedding αντι να χρησιμοποιουν πολλαπλασιασμο πινακων.

Κατασκευη ενος Στρωματος Embedding σε Στυλ PyTorch

Στο PyTorch, θα χρησιμοποιουσατε nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim). Ας κατασκευασουμε τη δικη μας εκδοχη απο την αρχη για να καταλαβουμε ακριβως τι συμβαινει εσωτερικα:

import numpy as np

class Embedding:
 """A simple embedding layer, similar to PyTorch's nn.Embedding."""

 def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
 """
 Args:
 num_embeddings: Size of the vocabulary (V)
 embedding_dim: Dimension of each embedding vector (d)
 """
 self.num_embeddings = num_embeddings
 self.embedding_dim = embedding_dim
 # Initialize weights randomly (Xavier/Glorot-like initialization)
 scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
 self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale

 def forward(self, token_ids):
 """
 Look up embeddings for the given token IDs.

 Args:
 token_ids: list or array of integer token IDs
 Returns:
 numpy array of shape (len(token_ids), embedding_dim)
 """
 return self.weight[token_ids]

 def __repr__(self):
 return f"Embedding({self.num_embeddings}, {self.embedding_dim})"

# === Demo: Using our Embedding layer ===
np.random.seed(123)

# GPT-2 uses vocab_size=50257, embed_dim=768
# We will use smaller values for demonstration
vocab_size = 10
embed_dim = 6

emb_layer = Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
print(f"Layer: {emb_layer}")
print(f"Weight matrix shape: {emb_layer.weight.shape}")

# Simulate a tokenized sentence: "The cat sat on the mat"

print(f"Embedding for token 2 (second occurrence): {output[4].round(3)}")

# In GPT-2:
print(f"\
--- GPT-2 Scale ---")
print(f"Vocabulary size: 50,257 tokens")
print(f"Embedding dimension: 768")
print(f"Embedding matrix parameters: {50257 * 768:,} = ~38.6 million!")

Διαστασεις Embedding και η Σημασια τους

Η διασταση του embedding (d) ειναι μια κρισιμη υπερπαραμετρος. Καθοριζει ποση πληροφορια μπορει να μεταφερει καθε embedding token. Συνηθισμενες επιλογες στην πραξη:

Μοντελο Διασταση Embedding Μεγεθος Λεξιλογιου Παραμετροι Embedding
GPT-2 Small 768 50.257 38,6M
GPT-2 Medium 1.024 50.257 51,5M
GPT-2 Large 1.280 50.257 64,3M
GPT-3 12.288 50.257 617,6M

Υψηλοτερες διαστασεις επιτρεπουν στο μοντελο να αποτυπωσει πιο λεπτες σχεσεις, αλλα αυξανουν επισης τη χρηση μνημης και τον χρονο υπολογισμου. Σκεφτειτε το σαν την αναλυση μιας φωτογραφιας: περισσοτερα pixels αποτυπωνουν περισσοτερες λεπτομερειες, αλλα με κοστος σε μεγεθος αρχειου.

Πως τα Embeddings Αποτυπωνουν Σημασιολογικες Σχεσεις

Μετα την εκπαιδευση, τα embeddings αναπτυσσουν αξιοσημειωτες ιδιοτητες. Το πιο διασημο παραδειγμα ειναι η αναλογια king–queen:

vector("king") - vector("man") + vector("woman") ≈ vector("queen")

Αυτο λειτουργει επειδη ο χωρος των embeddings οργανωνει τις εννοιες κατα μηκος σημαντικων κατευθυνσεων. Η διαφορα king - man αποτυπωνει την εννοια της "βασιλειας", και προσθετοντας την στο woman παιρνουμε το γυναικειο βασιλικο ισοδυναμο.

def cosine_sim(a, b):
 return np.dot(a, b) / (np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b))

# The famous analogy: king - man + woman = ?
result = embeddings["king"] - embeddings["man"] + embeddings["woman"]
print("=== King - Man + Woman = ? ===")
print(f"Result vector: {result}")
print(f"Queen vector: {embeddings['queen']}")
print(f"Similarity to queen: {cosine_sim(result, embeddings['queen']):.4f}")

# Find the closest word to the result
print("\
=== Closest words to result ===")
for word, vec in embeddings.items():
 sim = cosine_sim(result, vec)
 print(f" {word:<8} similarity: {sim:.4f}")

# Show that similar concepts cluster
print("\
=== Semantic Similarities ===")
pairs = [("king", "queen"), ("cat", "dog"), ("king", "table"),
 ("man", "woman"), ("cat", "table")]
for w1, w2 in pairs:
 sim = cosine_sim(embeddings[w1], embeddings[w2])
 print(f" sim({w1:<6}, {w2:<6}) = {sim:.4f}")

Οπτικοποιηση Embeddings σε 2D

Αν και τα πραγματικα embeddings ζουν σε εκατονταδες διαστασεις, μπορουμε να τα προβαλουμε σε 2D για να οπτικοποιησουμε τη δομη ομαδοποιησης. Τεχνικες οπως το PCA (Principal Component Analysis) η το t-SNE χρησιμοποιουνται συχνα για αυτο. Ακολουθει μια απλη προσεγγιση οπτικοποιησης βασισμενη στο PCA:

Συνδεση με το Βιβλιο

Στο Κεφαλαιο 2 του "Build an LLM from Scratch", ο Raschka υλοποιει το στρωμα token embedding ως το πρωτο συστατικο του μοντελου GPT. Η διασταση embedding (d_model η cfg["emb_dim"]) διαρρεει σε ολοκληρη την αρχιτεκτονικη — καθε επομενο στρωμα (προσοχη, feed-forward) λειτουργει σε διανυσματα αυτης της ιδιας διαστασης.

Κατασκευη Embeddings για τον Tokenizer μας

Ας συνδεσουμε το στρωμα embedding με τον BPE tokenizer που κατασκευασαμε στις προηγουμενες διαλεξεις. Αυτος ειναι ακριβως ο τροπος που το GPT-2 επεξεργαζεται την εισοδο του:

Python
import numpy as np

class SimpleTokenizer:
 """Minimal word-level tokenizer for demonstration."""
 def __init__(self, vocab):
 self.str_to_int = vocab
 self.int_to_str = {v: k for k, v in vocab.items()}

 def encode(self, text):
 tokens = text.lower().split()
 return [self.str_to_int.get(t, self.str_to_int.get("<unk>", 0))
 for t in tokens]

 def decode(self, ids):
 return " ".join(self.int_to_str.get(i, "<unk>") for i in ids)

class Embedding:
 def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
 scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
 self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale

 def forward(self, token_ids):
 return self.weight[np.array(token_ids)]

# Step 1: Create a vocabulary
vocab = {
 "<unk>": 0, "<pad>": 1, "the": 2, "cat": 3, "sat": 4,
 "on": 5, "mat": 6, "dog": 7, "ran": 8, "to": 9, "a": 10,
 "big": 11, "small": 12, "red": 13, "blue": 14, "house": 15
}

# Step 2: Initialize tokenizer and embedding layer
np.random.seed(42)
tokenizer = SimpleTokenizer(vocab)
embed_dim = 8
token_embedding = Embedding(len(vocab), embed_dim)

# Step 3: Process text through the pipeline
text = "the big cat sat on a red mat"
print(f"Input text: '{text}'")

token_ids = tokenizer.encode(text)
print(f"Token IDs: {token_ids}")
print(f"Decoded: '{tokenizer.decode(token_ids)}'")

# Step 4: Get embeddings
embeddings = token_embedding.forward(token_ids)
print(f"\
Embeddings shape: {embeddings.shape}")
print(f" (sequence_length={len(token_ids)}, embed_dim={embed_dim})")

print(f"\
First 3 token embeddings:")
for i in range(3):
 word = tokenizer.int_to_str[token_ids[i]]
 print(f" '{word}' (id={token_ids[i]}): {embeddings[i].round(3)}")

print(f"\
--- Pipeline Summary ---")
print(f"Text -> Tokens -> IDs -> Embeddings")
print(f"'{text}'")
print(f" -> {text.lower().split()}")
print(f" -> {token_ids}")
print(f" -> tensor of shape {embeddings.shape}")
Σημαντικη Σημειωση

Κατα την αρχικοποιηση, τα embeddings ειναι τυχαια! Δεν μεταφερουν καμια σημασια ακομα. Η μαγεια συμβαινει κατα την εκπαιδευση, οταν το μοντελο προσαρμοζει αυτα τα διανυσματα μεσω backpropagation για να ελαχιστοποιησει τη συναρτηση απωλειας. Μετα απο εκπαιδευση σε αρκετα δεδομενα, τα embeddings οργανωνονται φυσικα στη σημαντικη γεωμετρικη δομη που περιγραψαμε.

Περιληψη

Βασικα Συμπερασματα

  • Τα Token IDs ειναι αυθαιρετοι ακεραιοι χωρις σημασιολογικη σημασια
  • Τα embeddings ειναι πυκνα διανυσματα που αποτυπωνουν σχεσεις λεξεων
  • Το στρωμα embedding ειναι ενας απλος πινακας αναζητησης (πινακας)
  • Οι διαστασεις embedding ειναι μια βασικη υπερπαραμετρος (GPT-2: 768)
  • Μετα την εκπαιδευση, παρομοιες λεξεις καταληγουν κοντα η μια στην αλλη στον χωρο embedding

Τι Ακολουθει

Τωρα εχουμε embeddings για καθε token, αλλα το μοντελο μας δεν εχει εννοια σειρας λεξεων. Το embedding για το "cat" ειναι το ιδιο ειτε εμφανιζεται πρωτο ειτε τελευταιο σε μια προταση. Στη Διαλεξη 11, θα προσθεσουμε positional embeddings για να λυσουμε αυτο το προβλημα.
